narration.full_text: Let's work through an example to see how we can evaluate trigonometric expressions using identities. We'll focus on expressions involving squared trigonometric ratios, which often simplify beautifully with the Pythagorean identity. Consider the expression: sine squared theta plus cosine squared theta. This is the fundamental Pythagorean identity, stating that sine squared theta plus cosine squared theta always equals one. This identity is incredibly useful for simplifying more complex trigonometric expressions. By recognizing this pattern, we can quickly reduce parts of an equation, making it much easier to solve or prove. So, when you encounter sine squared theta plus cosine squared theta, remember its value is simply one.
